protocol.note: this record performs no new measurement -- it assembles the EXP-B1 four-row column set (docs/HANDOFF-ENGINE.md:218-224, the D-071 100M-costed table's row labels) from already-committed 100M records, exactly as expB1-30m.json did for 30M. warmups/reps/ceilings above describe this assembly step itself (a single pass), not the underlying measurements -- each row's own protocol is unchanged from its source record (see rows.*.source). The columnar_scan row is null: that operator (aggregate_events / agg.rel_bucket) is refused by the cost guardrail at 100M, one of six unanticipated refusals at this scale -- see rows.columnar_scan.value_ms_reason. No value is estimated.

exp_b1.description: EXP-B1 / D-071's four-row column set (docs/HANDOFF-ENGINE.md §4, "100M, costed": store on disk, query-ready floor (VmHWM), columnar scan, version_history) at the 100M scale point, per docs/design/SCALE_BUILD_FORECAST_2026-09-15.md §4's expB1-{30,100}m.json layout. Every value below is read from a field already committed on main under benchmarks/scale-v1/ -- no new measurement was taken to produce this file. Unlike expB1-30m.json, the columnar_scan row is null: aggregate_events is refused by the cost guardrail at 100M (a new finding at this scale, not anticipated by the pre-registration; all 13 operators, including this one, executed at 30M).

store_on_disk.label: store on disk
store_on_disk.note: total_bytes is build_info.store_bytes.total_bytes as recorded; it exceeds manifest_bytes + segment_bytes (the store's own eventlog / working-copy overhead is not itemized further in the source record, so no additional breakdown is claimed here).

query_ready_floor.label: query-ready floor (VmHWM)
query_ready_floor.note: fresh read-only process, cold-opens the finished store and runs the 13-operator registry once each; VmHWM of that process. Job 213189, run once cleanly (no writer-lock race, no rerun needed -- the 30M lane's read_only=True fix was already in place). n_ok=6/13: 7 operators refused by the cost guardrail even at this floor probe (same guardrail as the scale-curve refusals below), which does not change the VmHWM figure -- the process still opened the store and ran every admitted query.

columnar_scan.label: columnar scan (aggregate_events, query id agg.rel_bucket)
columnar_scan.value_ms_reason: refused by the cost guardrail at 100M -- 'CostError: estimated cost for aggregate_events exceeds ceilings' -- one of six unanticipated refusals at this scale (all thirteen operators, including this one, executed at 30M: see expB1-30m.json's columnar_scan row, 176.492 ms). No numeric time_est_ms is carried in the record for this refusal (unlike reach.window's dedicated admission probe), so none is reported here -- left null, not estimated, per this file's own no-new-measurement rule.
columnar_scan.note: "columnar scan" is this operator's label in docs/TECHNICAL_REPORT.md's D-058-vs-D-069 comparison ("columnar control (aggregate_events)"), reused here as the HANDOFF-ENGINE table's third row, same as expB1-30m.json. See osdiB7RefusedAggRelBucket100M in scripts/osdi_paper_macros.py::compute_b7_scale.

version_history.label: version_history (post D-069)
version_history.note: single_run (job 213191, no clean/contended split needed at 100M -- the whole chain ran serialized with nothing else touching the store), median over 3 reps of wall_ms and vmhwm_kb.
